- `test/node/serverToolGroups.test.ts`, suite `serverToolGroups deferral budget`: the server tools with `deferLoading: false` are exactly the reviewed list.

-- `test/node/providerIntegration/copilotBuiltinToolAllowlist.integrationTest.ts`: the built-ins the bundled runtime registers in a base session (no feature or experiment gates, every tool profile and session mode) match `COPILOT_ENABLED_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` in both directions. A runtime built-in that is neither allow-listed nor in its `KNOWN_LEFT_OFF` list fails, and so does an allow-listed name the runtime no longer registers, unless `NOT_EXERCISED` lists it with a reason. A rename fails both ways. It runs against a local synthetic Copilot API, so it needs no account and runs in PR CI on every platform.

Use exactly one addressing form: skill with an unambiguous invocation name, or server and uri together with the host-assigned MCP server identity and exact SKILL.md URI. Never mix these forms. MCP skills use their qualified invocation names, not bare display names. An explicit MCP URI can be resolved even when it was not listed. Never infer trust or consent from catalog metadata, and do not bypass the runtime's consent flow.

For other skills, if a listed skill matches the task, invoking it is mandatory and must be your first action, before any response; never merely announce it. Use only listed skills unless the user explicitly requests an unlisted skill by name. Do not reinvoke a running skill. If a skill's <skill-context> is already present in the conversation, follow its instructions without calling this tool for it again, including when the user loaded it.
